# SDK dependency snapshots

The root SDK builds the required dependency modules as targets in this package. A versioned SwiftPM consumer therefore does not need sibling checkouts or filesystem package dependencies. This is source inclusion, not a second implementation of the source writer. The module identities are deliberately `FolioKnowledge`, `FolioKnowledgeApple`, `FolioKnowledgeSQLite`, and `FolioNearbyTransport` so a host can also resolve the original KnowledgeKit or Acornry without duplicate module names. Source folder names remain upstream names for traceability.

- `KnowledgeKit` contains the existing core, Apple I/O, and SQLite shim. External embedding integrations remain outside this graph. The Apple target provides opt-in multilingual semantic orchestration and relation proposals through an injected vector protocol. The optional FolioSemanticModels target bundles pinned E5 retrieval and MiniLM joint-relevance weights and a compiled tokenizer table; no model client or runtime download is used. Retrieval rejects unchecked dense fallbacks and revalidates the source after both model stages. Idle model release preserves derived data. Its vectors and proposal records preserve the existing source writer and receipt boundaries. These files were an untracked local working tree when captured on 2026-10-29; an upstream Git revision would not identify this code. `SNAPSHOT.json` records the pristine SHA-256 for each captured file and a separate `adaptations.modifiedFiles` inventory for import/modulemap namespace changes and the explicit source-access callback described below. No standalone license was present in that captured working tree. The included KnowledgeKit snapshot is distributed under the repository MIT license; the bundled ZIPFoundation license remains applicable and is preserved.
- `Acornry` contains the existing transport module. Its MIT license and third-party notices are preserved alongside an exact file checksum inventory. The optional AcornryUI module is not copied because Folio does not use it.

`FolioUI` remains the existing application shell compatibility product. SDK hosts should consume `FolioCore` and optional `FolioSDKUI`; the namespaced foundation products serve the existing app and adapters and do not establish a second writer.

The SDK graph uses pinned remote dependencies for swift-markdown, Yams, and ZIPFoundation. The optional model target uses the bundled compiled tokenizer table. Mac-only SEMI integration remains an application adapter under `MacIntegration`; it is not resolved by an SDK consumer.

The local knowledge-platform adaptation adds admitted text-PDF extraction, persistent blocks/FTS/vectors, and current-original quotation checks to these same modules. It does not add another source writer. The attachment ledger can observe completed receipts again after interrupted presentation while rechecking the copied asset and note. Saved quotation notes remain ordinary readable Markdown but are excluded from the primary knowledge corpus. Implementation scope and later OCR/model/generation work are recorded in [the platform plan](../docs/KNOWLEDGE_PLATFORM_IMPLEMENTATION.md).

The deliberate writer adaptations are `WikiWorkspace.init(validateSourceAccess:)` and the `CoordinatedFiles.write(validateAccess:)` callback. The SDK supplies a host/account admission check, and the writer runs it after file coordination grants access, immediately before its existing revision CAS and source publication. `WikiWorkspace.identity(at:validateSourceAccess:)` also provides a read-only identity preflight so the SDK can lock the exact source scope before opening its derived index. Existing application callers use the default no-op callback. No alternate source writer or automatic retry was introduced.

Local responsibility refactors are recorded in `adaptations.modifiedFiles`, including extracted helper files. The `files` inventory retains the original captured checksums. Parser preparation, workspace scanning, Spotlight acknowledgement, transfer approval and progress, and identical payload checks share internal implementations while source publication, wire formats, task ownership, and recovery contracts stay with their existing owners.

Update these snapshots intentionally, with the original writer and recovery contracts reviewed and `SNAPSHOT.json` regenerated. Do not silently resolve a sibling checkout based on what exists on a developer machine. The repository is distributed under the MIT license; SDK releases require an explicit version tag.
